question: Where was the vast majority of healthcare delivered before the establishment of modern hospitals?
explanation: Early healthcare relied heavily on domestic environments where family and community members provided necessary remedies and nursing care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h1)

question: What primary role did religious and charitable groups play in early home nursing?

options.A: Building high-tech surgical suites inside local parishes
options.B: Manufacturing herbal drugs for commercial export
options.C: Enforcing strict medical licensing laws for healers
options.D: Sending volunteers to care for the sick poor at home

explanation: Charitable and religious organizations historically filled gaps by dispatching individuals to tend to vulnerable populations who lacked access to other facilities. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h1)

question: What was the main focus of early district and visiting nurses during the social reform era?
explanation: Visiting nurses focused heavily on community hygiene and communicable diseases to improve the living conditions of impoverished urban populations. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why did visiting nurses require a high degree of clinical autonomy?

options.A: They were legally permitted to practice medicine without a physician
options.B: They worked independently outside the direct supervision of a hospital
options.C: They had unlimited financial resources to purchase supplies
options.D: They only treated patients with minor, self-limiting conditions

explanation: Providing care inside patients' homes meant visiting nurses frequently had to make critical independent decisions without immediate medical backup. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h2)

question: What key change occurred with the establishment of formal home health agencies?

options.A: Home visits by nurses were completely prohibited by law
options.B: All home care services were taken over by private physicians
options.C: Care became organized into structured, multidisciplinary services
options.D: Nursing documentation and records were eliminated

explanation: Formal agencies brought structure, standardizing operations and bringing in diverse professional roles to coordinate patient care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h3)

question: How did the rise of formal agencies change the perception of home health care?

options.A: It made home care exclusively available to the wealthiest citizens
options.B: It reduced the quality of clinical documentation
options.C: It shifted from a charity gesture to a recognized healthcare component
options.D: It eliminated the need for trained nurses in domestic settings

explanation: Structuring home care into formal agencies elevated it into a legitimate, professional sector of health service delivery. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h3)

question: What major benefit did government funding bring to the home health sector?

options.A: Guaranteed retirement pensions for all nursing staff
options.B: Sustainable financial support for patient care services
options.C: Elimination of all charting requirements for nurses
options.D: Free medical equipment for every citizen globally

explanation: Government insurance and policy funding ensured that agencies could rely on consistent reimbursement for providing skilled care to patients. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h4)

question: What common challenge accompanied the introduction of formal government reimbursement rules?

options.A: A complete drop in the number of patients seeking home care
options.B: Heavy administrative burdens and strict documentation requirements
options.C: The total abolition of registered nurses in community settings
options.D: Unrestricted spending allowances for any medical supply

explanation: To qualify for funding, agencies must adhere to rigid criteria, forcing nurses to spend significant time on detailed compliance paperwork. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which tool has directly bridged the gap between hospital-level monitoring and home care?

options.C: Standard manual blood pressure cuffs only

explanation: Advanced portable equipment and remote tracking tools allow clinicians to monitor patient status closely outside hospital walls. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h5)

question: What impact do modern medical technologies have on patient length of stay in hospitals?

options.A: They allow patients with complex needs to be discharged home earlier
options.B: They eliminate the need for any inpatient hospital admissions whatsoever
options.C: They force patients to remain hospitalized for longer observation periods
options.D: They have no noticeable effect on how long patients stay admitted

explanation: Advanced home tech makes it safe to transition medically complex individuals out of costly inpatient units sooner. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h5)

question: What traditional system has historically formed the foundation of home care in Nigeria?
explanation: Nigerian care traditions heavily rely on family and community structures to support the sick and elderly at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which financial barrier commonly affects formal home health care access in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive taxation on all community nursing supplies
options.B: Mandatory prepayment for all hospital admissions
options.C: Reliance on out-of-pocket payments by patients and families
options.D: Strict international tariffs on home care equipment

explanation: Without widespread universal health insurance coverage, most families pay directly out of pocket for private home nursing services. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h6)

question: What demographic shift is primarily driving the increased global demand for home health nursing?

options.A: Aging populations and rising chronic illnesses
options.B: A sudden decline in overall birth rates worldwide
options.C: The complete eradication of infectious diseases
options.D: Mass migration of urban populations to rural areas

explanation: An older global population living longer with chronic conditions creates a massive, ongoing need for home-based clinical support. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which factor represents a distinct operational challenge unique to home health nursing compared to hospital nursing?

options.A: Navigating safety and security risks within community environments
options.B: Having immediate access to an on-site multidisciplinary medical team
options.C: Operating in strictly controlled, sterile hospital wards
options.D: Relying entirely on fixed wall oxygen outlets

explanation: Home nurses travel to varied, uncontrolled neighborhood settings, presenting safety challenges that do not exist inside a secure hospital. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T2#GNS324_U1_T2_h7)
